name: Skin bleaching injections (glutathione IV)
lead: Glutathione is a small antioxidant molecule made naturally by the body. It is promoted, in oral, topical and intravenous (IV) forms, as a skin-lightening agent, and IV or injected versions are sometimes sold as "whitening drips" [1][2]. Wikipedia describes glutathione as the most common agent taken by mouth to whiten skin [2].

A 2016 review in the Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology concluded that the evidence for efficacy and safety diverges, that no evidence proves IV glutathione works for skin lightening, and that adverse effects from IV use led the Philippine drug regulator to issue a warning [1]. Wikipedia likewise says it is unclear whether glutathione works and notes that the Philippine government advises against IV use [2]. In looksmaxxing communities it is sometimes discussed as a way to lighten skin tone or undertones [3].
infobox: Lighter skin tone via reduced melanin production
Philippine authorities warn against IV use [1][2]

paras: The review states that glutathione's lightening effect is attributed to direct and indirect inhibition of the enzyme tyrosinase and to a shift from eumelanin (dark pigment) to phaeomelanin (lighter pigment) production [1].

The 2016 review found a gap between how widely IV glutathione is used and the evidence supporting it, stating that no evidence proves efficacy for skin lightening and raising the possibility that its promotion is commercially driven [1]. Wikipedia says whether glutathione works remains unclear as of 2019 and lists it among whiteners that may contain harmful ingredients [2].

Skin lightening is widespread in parts of Asia, Africa and elsewhere, and glutathione is among the products used [2]. A forum thread on looksmax.org asks whether glutathione injections clear skin undertones, with one poster reporting that their eyes looked lighter after a first IV session [3].

No studies found establishing efficacy of IV glutathione for skin lightening; the 2016 review states that no evidence proves it [1]. Registered trials involving glutathione concern other conditions, such as gingival hyperpigmentation [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, glutathione IV is discussed as a possible way to lighten skin tone or clear undertones [3].

claims.claim: Glutathione IV lightens skin and clears undertones.
claims.believers: One poster reported lighter eyes after a first session, and others reasoned that it works because it is a potent antioxidant [3].
claims.experts: A 2016 dermatology review found no evidence proving IV glutathione is effective for lightening and noted regulator warnings in the Philippines [1].

card.summary: IV glutathione sold as whitening drips; reviewers found no evidence that it lightens skin and a regulator has warned against it.
card.note: Philippine authorities advise against IV use.

quick.overview:
Glutathione is an antioxidant the body makes. Some clinics sell it as intravenous "whitening drips" to lighten skin.

A 2016 review found no evidence proving IV glutathione is effective for this purpose.
quick.mechanism: It is said to inhibit tyrosinase and shift melanin production toward lighter pigment.
quick.risks: The Philippine drug regulator warned against IV use after adverse effects; evidence for safety and efficacy is limited.
